title.narrative: CORE - Community-driven Opportunities for Resilience and Empowerment in Syria

description.narrative: Objective: Strengthening community resilience for inclusive development and improved food security in Syria

Project objective is that vulnerable communities in Syria achieve greater self-reliance, food security, and social cohesion. Enhanced knowledge of nutrition and food systems leads to improved health and well-being, while strengthened legal awareness empowers individuals to secure their property rights. The establishment of community-based organizations fosters a safer environment by addressing gender-based violence and promoting peaceful coexistence. Economic development through income-generating activities contributes to long-term resilience, reducing dependence on humanitarian aid and enhancing overall stability in affected communities. Activities belonging to the goal contribute to several sustainable goals: SGD 1., SGD 2., SGD 5., SDG 17.

Returnees and displaced people: Residents of camps and informal settlements in northwest Syria have either returned or are planning to relocate in short to mid-term future to their places of origin or settled in the host communities. Youth (IDPs and host community members): With limited access to educational opportunities over the last decade created by the war/post-war conditions of lack of institutional capacities, youth in Syria are facing lack of necessary skills that match the market demands, as well as access to any sustainable employment opportunities. Women (IDPs and host community members): One in five households are headed by women. These women are navigating profound instability in a context where female unemployment exceeds 80 percent and social safety nets have largely disappeared. PwDs: (internally displaced persons, host/rural communities) are rarely integrated into economic activities and decision-making bodies, which results in a high level of vulnerability and dependence on their household members.
